Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (oral lesions)

Small reports describe improvement in oral lesions treated with PBM plus cord-blood platelet gel. No PBM-only comparison isolates the light treatment.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Small reports describe improvement in oral lesions treated with PBM plus cord-blood platelet gel. No PBM-only comparison isolates the light treatment.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact category contains one human case series (seven patients, 19 oral lesions). One adjacent oral inherited-epidermolysis-bullosa split-mouth report (34 lesions) is relevant but is not specifically indexed as dystrophic EB; the same investigators and platelet-gel/PBM combination mean patient overlap cannot be excluded. No controlled PBM-only study is listed.

Human and clinical evidence

In the exact-category series, pain and lesion size improved during treatment, and treated sites were lesion-free at later visits, while lesions continued at untreated sites. The adjacent report also described improvement after cord-blood platelet gel plus PBM. Because both reports used platelet gel alongside light treatment and samples were small, they do not establish PBM's independent effect (Sindici et al. 2017, 2020). The 34-lesion split-mouth count is a lesion-level denominator rather than an independent patient sample. Neither publication compares PBM plus platelet gel with platelet gel alone, so synergy and attribution remain unresolved. The evidence supports feasibility for treated oral lesions only, not systemic disease control, skin-wound outcomes, long-term recurrence prevention, or a standardized regimen.

Primary original studies: Sindici et al. 2017 Sindici et al. 2020

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The 2017 case series reports 904 nm near-infrared treatment at 28.4 J/cm² for 900 seconds, over 3 treatment days, alongside cord-blood platelet gel. The 2020 report also used PBM with platelet gel. Lesion counts are not independent patient counts, and no common PBM-only protocol can be inferred from these combined-treatment studies.

Interpretation

These reports support feasibility in selected oral lesions, not systemic disease control or a proven PBM-specific effect. The platelet-gel co-treatment, small samples, short follow-up, and possible patient overlap limit causal interpretation. The findings do not establish prevention of recurrence, a standardized regimen, or effects on skin lesions.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. PBM was combined with platelet gel, so its independent effect is unknown.
Publications and records2 unique titles.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact-category evidence is a seven-patient case series covering 19 oral lesions. A mapped split-mouth report also used cord-blood platelet gel with PBM and counted 34 lesions; patient overlap cannot be excluded. Improvement in these co-treated lesions does not show whether PBM adds benefit beyond platelet gel.
